sources.title: 権(ケン)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク
sources.summary_en: Digital Daijisen lists 権 as both power to control others and a qualification to act or make claims. Kokusho Daijiten also records senses related to rights, including a qualification to act and a right attached to an office.

sources.title: 受容期における人格概念の内実としての権利・義務概念――その関係依存的解釈と関係規定的解釈：西周を例として
sources.summary_en: Hiroshi Goto’s 2023 scholarly article discusses the modern Japanese adoption of 権利 as a translation for right. It reports that Nishi and Tsuda consulted William Martin’s Chinese translation of Wheaton’s Elements of International Law. It describes Martin’s account that 利 was added because 権 could refer either to officials’ authority or to what ordinary people were due, while noting that the intended nuance of 権利 admits more than one interpretation. This historical discussion does not prove a fixed, transparent modern Japanese component-by-component derivation.

claims.text_en: In modern Japanese, 権利 can mean a qualification or capacity to act freely or make a demand. In legal usage it can mean the capacity to claim and enjoy a benefit. The cited literary example uses the general qualification sense: the first finder has the right to eat the food.

権 has an attested Japanese sense meaning a qualification or capacity to act or make a claim, alongside the distinct sense of power or authority. Thus “power” alone does not cover its relevant association in 権利.

利 is associated in Japanese character references with usefulness, advantage, and profit or gain. These associations are compatible with the benefit that may be claimed or enjoyed under a right, but the references do not establish that 利 independently means “entitlement” in 権利.

A scholarly account of the term’s modern Japanese adoption reports that Martin’s translation added 利 to 権 in a context where 権 alone could suggest officials’ authority, and describes 利 as helping express what ordinary people were due. The same account presents more than one interpretation of the choice, so it does not establish a single proven compositional derivation for modern Japanese 権利.

The dictionary’s older gloss “power and benefit,” its general modern sense, and its legal sense identified as a translation of English right are distinct evidence. The older gloss by itself does not prove that modern 権利 was formed by simply combining the standalone meanings “power” and “benefit.”

sources.title: 先生（読み）センセイ | コトバンク
sources.summary_en: Opened the page containing both Digital Daijisen and Seisenban Nihon Kokugo Daijiten entries. Digital Daijisen explicitly labels the sense “a person born before oneself; an elder” as 原義 (original sense), and separately gives the teacher sense. Seisenban Nihon Kokugo Daijiten records Japanese attestations for a scholar around 900, an elder around 1223–24, a teacher or master in 1786, and respectful address in 1763. The entry supports the existence of these senses and Daijisen’s account of the elder sense as original; its listed attestations alone do not establish a complete path of semantic change.

sources.title: センセイ | 言葉 | 漢字ペディア
sources.summary_en: Opened the compound entry, which lists teacher, expert honorific, elder, and joking or familiar address senses. It confirms the sense inventory but gives no account of how the teacher sense developed from the elder sense.

claims.text_en: The component gloss is linguistically plausible: Japanese kanji references give 先 meanings such as “earlier in time” and 生 meanings including “to be born.” These are character-level contributions, not proof by themselves of the compound’s historical formation.

“A person born earlier; an elder” is an attested Japanese sense of 先生, and Digital Daijisen explicitly identifies it as the original sense. Thus, presenting “born earlier” as a conventional explanation has lexicographic support and is not merely an invented folk gloss. The opened evidence does not prove that every component-level paraphrase is a historical derivation.

The historical dictionary records an attestation for the scholar sense around 900, earlier than its cited elder-sense attestation around 1223–24; it records teacher/master use in 1786 and respectful address in 1763. Those dated examples document usage, but do not by themselves show that the elder sense developed into the teacher sense. In particular, the proposed bridge “earlier in learning” is an inference not supported by the opened sources.

For a reusable explanation of the modern teacher sense, it is supported to say that 先生 means teacher/instructor and that the characters can be read as “earlier” plus “born”; if included, qualify “born earlier” as the dictionary-identified original sense. Do not claim that teachers are called this because they were born earlier, are ahead in learning, or follow a specific proven semantic pathway.

senses.definition: expresses that something is not necessarily the case; it is not that…

meaning_guide.explanation_en: After a plain-form clause, わけではない says that the clause is not necessarily true or does not follow as a conclusion; it often qualifies an assumption without asserting the opposite. わけ frames the clause as an explanation or conclusion, and ではない denies that interpretation. With a noun or な-adjective, use な before わけ, as in 学生なわけではない.

parts.contribution_en: Frames the preceding statement as an explanation or conclusion.

sources.title: 「熱中」とは？意味や例文や読み方や由来について解説！
sources.summary_en: This secondary word-explanation page claims 熱中 combines 熱 ('passion') and 中 ('inside/middle') to evoke being in the midst of heat, and makes historical claims about a modern Japanese coinage. It supplies no supporting linguistic references for those claims. It is recorded as a conflicting unsupported account, not used as evidence for the analysis.

claims.text_en: Modern Japanese dictionaries define 熱中 as deeply directing one’s attention to something or becoming engrossed, and give examples of being absorbed in an activity. This supports the supplied sense and its use with activities or interests.

熱 independently has modern Japanese dictionary senses involving mental concentration, commitment, and absorption; the dictionary also groups 熱中 with those senses. 熱 can therefore be described cautiously as associated with mental intensity or ardor in this compound, although the dictionary does not state a precise compositional analysis.

The consulted dictionary describes 中 in other compounds with general meanings such as being within a spatial or temporal range and includes 夢中 as an example. It does not establish that 中 contributes ‘inside,’ ‘within,’ or ‘immersed’ to 熱中; assigning that contribution would remain an inference.
The dictionary attestation from 布令字弁 and the later literary example document historical uses of 熱中. They do not by themselves prove a historical derivation from the separate meanings of 熱 and 中.

claims.text_en: 後架 is a recorded Japanese term for both a Zen temple washroom behind the monks' hall and, by extension, a toilet; the dictionary explains the latter sense by the toilet's proximity to the washroom. It also records an older, narrower sense, “urinal.”

In 吾輩は猫である, 後架 in 後架先生 points to the place where the man sings: the text says he sings inside 後架 and is nicknamed 後架先生 by people nearby. The text and dictionary together support reading 後架 here as toilet-related, not as an inferred historical derivation.

An architectural glossary presents an account in which an exterior 縁 becomes enclosed by doors and is then called 縁側. This offers context for the architectural term, but it is not evidence for the word's historical derivation or for the spelling 椽側.

claims.text_en: For the modern Japanese word あくび meaning “a yawn,” dictionaries record 欠伸 and 欠 as spellings. Digital Daijisen derives あくび from the continuative form of あくぶ. That account supports a word-level connection to あくぶ; it does not establish a two-character formation in which 欠 and 伸 separately contribute to the reading あくび.

欠 has a relevant yawn sense under the reading ケン, distinct from the character 欠 used for 缺 in the sense “lack.” Therefore “lack” is not an appropriate component gloss for the 欠 in 欠伸 when referring to the yawn word.

In the separate reading けんしん, dictionaries define 欠伸 as yawning and stretching; 欠 has a yawn sense and 伸 means extend or stretch. This supports those component meanings for that compound reading, but does not demonstrate that 伸 contributes reliably to the modern lexical meaning of あくび.

The Buddhist association of 魔 with demons and obstacles is historically relevant: Japanese dictionaries describe 魔 as an abbreviation of 魔羅, a transcription of Sanskrit māra, and include Buddhist meanings such as an impediment to awakening. This supports a historical bridge from Buddhist obstruction to the general hindrance sense, but does not show that 魔 independently supplies the full modern meaning in every use.

A cautious modern component gloss is: 退 suggests retreating or withdrawing; 屈 can suggest bending, yielding, or losing resolve. sources.summary_en: Huang and Ochi describe Japanese ittai questions as implying speaker impatience or annoyance. They analyze ittai as an adverb associated with a wh-phrase and an interrogative attitude. This supports a pragmatic description of the whole adverb, not a decomposition into the meanings of its written components.

sources.title: 「いったい」という副詞について - 武庫川女子大学リポジトリ
sources.summary_en: The accessible repository record provides Yutaka Yamaguchi’s abstract. It reports a study of uses in Meiji, Taisho, and early Showa literary works; the abstract says the author distinguishes generalizing and emphatic-question uses from a further retrospective use glossed roughly as 'in the first place' or 'really,' and reports that the frequencies of these uses change over time. The abstract does not provide the study’s examples or detailed argument.

sources.title: 「一体」の歴史的変遷と変化の類型性 - NDL Search
sources.summary_en: The National Diet Library record identifies Yao Yao’s 2022 article in 国語学研究, pages 182–196, and lists subject terms including adverbialization and questioning. The opened record supplies bibliographic metadata only, not the article’s argument or evidence.

claims.text_en: In the interrogative-adverb use, 一体 marks strong questioning and may convey reproach. In the supplied example, it emphasizes the question asking what the addressee is; the dictionaries’ matching sense supports a reusable explanation such as 'what on earth?' or 'what exactly?' rather than separate translations for 一 and 体.

A linguistic analysis likewise treats ittai as an adverb in questions and associates it with an attitude such as impatience or annoyance. That analysis concerns the word’s function, not a semantic contribution from each kanji.

The dictionary describes a usage path within 一体 as a whole: from a generalizing adverbial sense ('generally; in broad outline') to a use that especially strengthens a question or serves in reproach. It records an 1843 example of the questioning use. This supports historical development as relevant context, but does not by itself establish every step or mechanism.

Yamaguchi’s article abstract reports an additional retrospective use, roughly 'in the first place' or 'really,' in literary works from the Meiji, Taisho, and early Showa periods, and says the frequencies of the reported uses change over time. Because only the abstract was available in the opened repository record, its detailed evidence cannot be assessed here.

senses.definition: to fear; to be afraid of

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 怖がる means “to be afraid of” or “to show fear of.” The suffix がる makes a verb from the adjective 怖い, describing someone who shows signs of fear; it often refers to another person’s or animal’s visible reaction.

parts.contribution_en: The stem of 怖い, expressing the quality of being frightening and, in this verb, the fear someone shows.
Makes a verb from an adjective stem, describing someone as showing signs of that quality or feeling.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 馬鹿にする combines 馬鹿 (“fool; foolish”) with にする, a pattern for treating someone as something. It means to treat someone as a fool and, in use, to mock or look down on them.

parts.contribution_en: fool; foolish
marks the status or role assigned to someone
forms the act of treating someone in that way

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 随分 means ‘quite,’ ‘very,’ or ‘considerably,’ marking a high degree. Japanese use developed from concrete quantity to abstract degree; it can also suggest that the degree is striking, sometimes with surprise or dissatisfaction. Older records include a sense related to one’s due share, but the modern degree meaning is not built by adding separate character meanings.

parts.contribution_en: In an older analysis, this means ‘follow’ or ‘accord with’ in relation to a share; its contribution to the modern degree meaning is not established.
In the older sense, this is compatible with ‘share’ or ‘status’; a distinct contribution to the modern degree meaning is not established.

meaning_guide.caveat_en: The older analysis relates 随 to ‘follow’ and 分 to ‘share’ or ‘status.’ The evidence does not establish distinct contributions from these characters to the modern degree meaning.

sources.title: 随分（読み）ズイブン — コトバンク; デジタル大辞泉 and 精選版 日本国語大辞典
sources.summary_en: The dictionaries record a noun sense ‘in keeping with one’s status or due portion,’ with a cited example dated circa 892; an adverbial sense ‘as much as one can’ cited to the early 13th century; and a degree-adverb sense ‘greatly, considerably, very,’ with an example from the early 13th century. Digital Daijisen also describes the modern degree use as often conveying surprise or dissatisfaction. These are lexicographic senses and dated citations, not by themselves proof of each transition between senses.

sources.title: 程度的意味・評価的意味の発生 : 漢語「随分」の受容と変容を例として — J-STAGE
sources.summary_en: The abstract by Shin’ichi Narumi describes a Japanese semantic path from concrete quantity-adverb use to abstract degree meaning and then evaluative meaning. It says the word originally lacked degree meaning. The article page links to the full paper, which was also opened.

sources.title: 程度的意味・評価的意味の発生 : 漢語「随分」の受容と変容を例として — full text PDF, J-STAGE
sources.summary_en: The opened full text calls 随分 a Sino-Japanese word and discusses older Chinese-language examples glossed as ‘according to one’s share/lot.’ It distinguishes this older sense from modern Japanese degree-adverb use and analyzes the Japanese semantic change through quantity-adverb use. This supports reporting the author’s historical analysis, but does not make each character’s gloss a transparent contribution to the modern degree sense.

sources.title: 随分／ずいぶん — 語源由来辞典
sources.summary_en: This secondary etymology page proposes the segmentation ‘分に随う’ and gives a sequence from ‘commensurate with one’s status’ through ‘as much as possible’ to ‘quite/very.’ It supplies no documentary argument on the opened page, so it is not independent proof of the derivation.

sources.title: 随 — 漢字一字 — 漢字ペディア
sources.summary_en: The entry gives 随 the Japanese reading したがう and character meanings including ‘follow’ and ‘do as one wishes.’ Character meanings offer context for a proposed segmentation, but do not demonstrate the compound’s modern compositional meaning or historical development.

sources.title: 分（読み）ブン — コトバンク; デジタル大辞泉 and 精選版 日本国語大辞典
sources.summary_en: The entries record 分 with senses including a divided share or portion, a person’s status or capacity, and an amount or degree. These senses are compatible with the older ‘one’s share/lot’ interpretation, but do not establish that 分 contributes a distinct ‘quite/very’ meaning in modern 随分.

claims.text_en: Japanese dictionaries record both an older noun sense of 随分 meaning ‘in keeping with one’s status or due portion’ and later adverb senses, including ‘as much as one can’ and ‘greatly/considerably/very.’ Their dated citations include circa 892 for the noun sense and early-13th-century examples for the adverb senses. The citations document recorded uses; they should not alone be presented as proof of a continuous step-by-step derivation.

Narumi’s scholarly study analyzes the Japanese development of 随分’s degree meaning as proceeding through a concrete quantity-adverb use, followed by abstract degree meaning and then evaluative meaning. This supplies a scholarly account of the bridge to modern ‘quite/very/considerably’; the modern degree use is not explained by simply adding character glosses.

The study discusses an older ‘according to one’s share/lot’ interpretation, and the Japanese dictionaries record a compatible older noun sense. The characters also have relevant standalone glosses: 随 can mean ‘follow,’ while 分 can mean ‘share/portion’ or ‘status.’ These facts make ‘分に随う’ an intelligible historical segmentation, but do not establish that the modern degree adverb retains separate, productive meanings for each component.

For the supplied example, 痩せている is modified by the degree-adverb sense of 随分. Digital Daijisen defines this use as ‘very/greatly/considerably’ and notes that it often carries a reaction such as surprise or dissatisfaction; the dictionary wording describes a tendency, not a required nuance in every occurrence.

senses.definition: to become thin; to lose weight

parts.contribution_en: Contributes “have” in the image of having a name.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 付き合う means to associate or socialize with someone, often by spending time in their company. 付き contributes joining or staying close to someone, while 合う adds doing something together or with one another; together they describe keeping company.

parts.contribution_en: The continuative form of 付く contributes joining or staying close to someone.
Adds doing something together or with one another.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: どちら asks which of two alternatives is meant. It directs attention to the choice between them.

senses.definition: superior in status or importance; great

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 偉い describes someone or something considered important or high in status. For a person, it often conveys respected standing.
尋ねる means to ask or inquire, usually by putting a question to someone to get information or an answer.

senses.definition: be certain; be sure to be

meaning_guide.explanation_en: に決まっている expresses emphatic certainty: the speaker presents something as settled or bound to be so. に marks what is settled upon, while 決まっている means “stands decided”; together they turn a decision or settled outcome into a confident judgment.

parts.contribution_en: Marks what is settled upon or determined to be the case.
Means “stands decided” or “is settled,” providing the image behind the construction’s certainty.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 骨（ほね）means a bone, the hard part of the skeleton. It can also refer collectively to the bones in a body.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 皮（かわ）means the skin covering a person or animal, or an animal’s hide.

component_uses.contribution_en: outer covering
skin

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 話し方 combines 話す, “to speak,” in the form 話し with 方（かた）, “way” or “manner.” It means the way someone speaks.

Adds an image of rolling or settling into a sprawled position; an actual tumble is not required.

senses.definition: a subordinate or follower, especially in a hierarchical relationship

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 子分 is someone in the child-side role of a 親分–子分 relationship: a subordinate who follows the 親分. In related family-role compounds, 分 can mark someone treated as a family member, which fits this pairing, though its precise contribution in 子分 is not directly specified.

parts.contribution_en: Marks the child-side role in relation to a 親分.
In related family-role compounds, marks someone treated as a family member; its precise contribution in 子分 is not directly specified.

claims.text_en: There is direct dictionary support for a modern family-role use of suffixal 分: NINJAL explains it as marking someone treated as, or pledged to act as, a named family relation, with examples including 兄貴分, 妹分 and 親分. This makes a child-side role reading for 子分 consistent with the dictionaries’ definitions of 子分 as an arranged child or a subordinate paired with 親分, but the NINJAL entry does not explicitly analyze 子分 itself.

The dictionaries define the follower sense relationally: 子分 follows or is subordinate to a 親分. The encyclopedia also equates 子分 with 子方 and 親分 with 親方, and describes protection alongside subordination in the social relationship. These descriptions support explaining the pair through child-side and parent-side social roles; they do not prove a historical derivation.

Nihon Kokugo Daijiten attests an arranged-child sense of 子分 in 1686 and a follower-of-a-親分 sense in 1773. These are attestations of usage, not evidence establishing how 子分 was coined or how its 分 component developed.

General dictionary discussion recognizes role or status among the meanings associated with 分, but it does not assign that specific sense to 子分 or 親分. Applying the general role/status meaning to these compounds as their proven etymology would go beyond the evidence.

兄弟分 is defined as a sibling-like relationship made between people who are not actual siblings. This supports the existence of a broader family-role pattern in compounds ending in 分, but does not by itself establish the precise contribution of 分 in 子分.

sources.summary_en: For 楽（らく）, Digital Daijisen gives a sense of being free of physical or mental discomfort and at ease, as well as a separate sense of being easy. The historical dictionary describes a peaceful, pleasant state without suffering or hardship. These definitions support an ease or relief-from-strain contribution; they do not specifically assign freedom from worry to 楽 by itself.

claims.text_en: In modern 気楽, 楽（らく） contributes the idea of being at ease or free of discomfort and hardship. The dictionaries also give 楽 a separate sense of ease in the sense of something being easy. 気楽 as a whole is explicitly defined as involving no worry or hardship and being relaxed. The evidence supports freedom from strain as compatible with 楽, while the specific wording about worry is attested for the whole compound, not established here as a distinct contribution of 楽 alone.

The dictionary definitions support a modern semantic comparison, not a proven account of the compound's historical formation. The 1813–23 example attests 気楽 by that period but does not establish its derivation.

sources.summary_en: Nippon Kokugo Daijiten defines 鼬の最後屁 as a weasel's escape by emitting a bad smell, figuratively a desperate expedient, and also a final disgraceful act. It cites an animal-image attestation from 1676 onward. Kotowaza o Shiru Jiten describes the figurative expression as an undesirable expedient or final disgrace, cites a 1902 example, and notes a disparaging nuance. Its explanation describes the animal's emission as foul-smelling liquid from glands near the anus; this is the dictionary's account of the idiom's image, not evidence that a weasel literally farts.

sources.summary_en: Defines 鼬の最後っ屁 as a desperate expedient at a crisis or a final harassment, and explains the expression through the weasel's foul-smelling escape behavior.

sources.summary_en: Digital Daijisen gives a standalone entry for 最後っ屁: the bad smell an animal emits when cornered, and, figuratively, a desperate measure or last resort. Its example is from Dazai Osamu's 「ロマネスク」.

claims.text_en: Modern dictionary senses of 屁 include gas expelled from the anus and, figuratively, something worthless or trivial. The latter sense is attested in expressions such as 「屁にもならない」; it does not show that 屁 contributes 'worthless' in every compound.

In 最後っ屁, 最後 contributes 'last/final'; 屁 evokes the familiar image of a fart or foul-smelling emission. This is a narrow explanation of the expression's image, not evidence that 屁 has a productive, general compound meaning. In the weasel expression, dictionaries describe the animal's defensive emission as a bad smell, with one explaining it as foul-smelling liquid from glands near the anus.

The figurative sense is lexicalized both in 鼬の最後屁 and in the standalone headword 最後っ屁: a desperate expedient or last resort. Dictionaries also record a related use for a final disgraceful act or harassment. The 1676 citation attests the animal image; the 1902 citation attests a figurative use of the weasel expression, but these dates do not by themselves establish when or how the figurative sense developed.

The figurative use often carries criticism or disparagement when it characterizes an undesirable expedient, final disgrace, or harassment. The dictionaries support those connotations, but do not establish that every use of standalone 最後っ屁 is disparaging.

sources.summary_en: The 精選版 日本国語大辞典 defines さかなや as a seller of edible fish and other seafood or the shop where they are sold. Its first cited example, from 1682, spells the compound 肴屋.

claims.text_en: In 肴屋 (さかなや), 肴 contributes the reading さかな and the fish or seafood sense: the dictionary defines さかなや as a seller of edible fish and other seafood or their shop, and its 1682 example writes the compound 肴屋. This supports the supplied ‘fish shop; fishmonger’ gloss. The compound evidence does not mean that standalone 肴 always means fish.
Standalone 肴 (さかな) has a distinct modern sense: food served with alcohol. It can also mean entertainment or a topic that enlivens a drinking gathering.

Japanese dictionaries give a conventional analysis of さかな as さか ‘酒’ plus な ‘side dish/food accompaniment’. They document the drinking-accompaniment sense and the later fish sense, with one dictionary explaining the latter by fish often being served as drinking food. This is a lexicographic account of the word’s semantic history; it does not establish a proven derivation or mean that 肴屋 refers to an alcoholic accompaniment.

sources.summary_en: The National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics dictionary distinguishes a valuable sense involving careful treatment from a very important sense, with examples for both. It supports modern sense coverage, not the role or history of 切.

claims.text_en: In modern Japanese, 大切 means something is highly important or worthy of regard, and it can describe treating something valuable with care. This matches the supplied examples’ senses “importance” and “valued.”

For the component question, the narrowest supported explanation is that 切 is conventionally associated here with pressing, earnest intensity or seriousness; it does not mean literal cutting in 大切. A Japanese character entry explicitly includes 大切 among examples under a pressing sense, while another reference lists 切’s pressing, earnest, and attentive senses without assigning 大切 to all of them.

The proposed explanation of 大切 as an intensifying 大 plus a pressing or urgent 切 is presented tentatively by a Japanese reference, which cautions that meanings changed over time. The dated whole-word attestations show an early urgent sense and later senses of importance and careful treatment, but chronology alone does not prove that this was the compound’s derivation or semantic path.

claims.text_en: In current Japanese, 経験 covers undergoing or directly encountering something and the knowledge or skill gained from it; 経験する means to experience or undergo something.

Dictionaries give 経る senses such as passing through a process, and 験 senses such as testing, evidence, or effect. These related senses do not by themselves establish that 経 and 験 make those separate contributions in modern 経験.

A historical study tentatively analyzes early 経験 as a verb-object formation, glossed as 験を経る (“pass through/test an efficacy”). It notes that 験 appears independently with the sense “efficacy/effect” in the cited medical text. This proposal concerns historical usage and does not establish the compound's definitive origin or its modern semantic composition.

claims.text_en: Japanese dictionaries support the supplied sense range: 都合 can refer to the conditions or circumstances affecting what someone does, whether those conditions suit, and arrangements. These uses fit the entry's broad circumstances/convenience sense.

Modern character references give 都 a character-level sense ‘all/everything’ and 合 senses including ‘join/combine,’ ‘gather,’ and ‘fit/correspond.’ The dictionaries also attest a 都合 sense ‘put together/total.’ These are plausible component associations for the total sense, but the references do not establish that 都 and 合 independently contribute those meanings to modern 都合 when it means circumstances or convenience.

The Nihon Kokugo Daijiten cites a 734 example for 都合 meaning combine or total, an 1789 example for arranging or procuring, and a 1790 example for situation or circumstances. These dated examples document the senses, but their sequence alone does not demonstrate that one sense historically developed from another.

語源由来辞典 explicitly proposes a historical path from totaling through arranging to circumstances or condition. This is a reported secondary etymological proposal, not a derivation independently demonstrated by the opened dictionary entries.

The opened modern word entries define the circumstances and suitability senses as whole-word meanings; the opened character entries establish possible character-level associations but do not analyze those meanings compositionally. Therefore, whether 都 and 合 have reliably recoverable, separate modern semantic contributions in the circumstances/convenience sense remains unresolved.

The article presents 元/gan and 來/rai as morphemes meaning ‘origin/beginning’ and ‘come,’ and discusses 来 as a temporal suffix in the history of Chinese yuánlái. sources.title: ガンライ | 言葉 | 漢字ペディア
sources.summary_en: The Japan Kanji Aptitude Testing Foundation’s Kanjipedia defines 元来 as ‘from the origin; from the beginning’ and gives an example about an inherently timid disposition. It supports the whole-word meaning, not a separate contribution by 来.

sources.title: 来(ライ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク
sources.summary_en: Digital Daijisen lists a general ライ sense meaning ‘from a past point up to the present’ and includes 元来 among examples. The Japanese National Language Dictionary likewise records ライ as a word-forming element that can indicate continuation from a time up to the present, with examples such as 数日来 and 昨年来. This establishes a broader pattern for ライ, but does not explicitly analyze its contribution within 元来.

claims.text_en: Japanese dictionaries support the whole-word meaning ‘from the beginning/originally,’ including a state or quality that has held from the start. A dictionary also records a distinct clause-initial use; the supplied example aligns with the core adverbial sense.

Yang reports early Japanese readings moto-yori (‘from the origin’) and hajime-yori (‘from the beginning’), followed later by the on-reading gwanrai. These readings provide a historical interpretive bridge for the compound, but do not by themselves demonstrate that modern ganrai is compositionally interpreted in every use.

Yang’s study analyzes modern ganrai as usually non-contrastive: ‘from the beginning till now/always,’ with an extension to ‘by nature/inherently.’ It also identifies a rarer contrastive temporal use meaning ‘originally’ or ‘previously.’ These are analyses of the whole Japanese word, not proof of a separate modern 来 meaning.

A Japanese dictionary records a broader ライ pattern meaning continuation from a past time up to the present, and lists 元来 as an example. This makes a temporal association for 来 plausible, but the entry does not establish how dependable or independently recoverable that contribution is in 元来 itself.

Yang describes 元/gan and 來/rai as morphemes meaning ‘origin/beginning’ and ‘come,’ and presents the Chinese form yuánlái as historically formed with a temporal lái suffix. This supports a proposed component-level bridge, but the article’s account of Chinese formation does not prove that 来 contributes the same distinct meaning in Japanese 元来.

The Japanese National Language Dictionary cites 元来 in a Shoku Nihongi passage dated 713 for the ‘previously/from the beginning’ sense. Yang independently reports entry into Japanese written texts around the eighth century. These attestations establish early written use, not the compound’s exact formation process.

sources.summary_en: Reports the proposals that 立派 derives from establishing a religious school or from Buddhist 立破文明. It elaborates those proposals but says the origin cannot be determined conclusively; this is a secondary etymology reference, not proof of either derivation.

claims.text_en: Japanese dictionaries define modern 立派 as a whole word meaning imposing or dignified, excellent, or complete without shortcomings. Their entries do not explain those modern senses as a direct combination of separate meanings of 立 and 派.

The major dictionary entries consulted give 派を立てる (“establish a school or faction”) as an account of 立派’s formation and mention 立破 as an alternative. These are reported etymological proposals, not evidence that the modern adjective compositionally means “stand + faction.”

立破 is separately recorded as a Buddhist term for establishing one's position and refuting another's; the dictionary also records a りっぱ reading and a 13th-century example. This establishes the term and reading in the historical record, but does not prove that the modern adjective derives from it.

A secondary etymology reference presents both the school-forming and 立破 accounts and says the origin cannot be decided conclusively. The evidence consulted therefore does not establish either proposed derivation or demonstrate that 立派 is chiefly a conventional spelling.

sources.title: 増長（読み）ゾウチョウ｜コトバンク（デジタル大辞泉・精選版 日本国語大辞典）
sources.summary_en: Digital Daijisen defines 増長 as a degree becoming more pronounced or someone becoming gradually haughty. The National Dictionary gives the same two senses and cites an example for general intensification from 宝物集 (c. 1179) and 日葡辞書 (1603–04) for the haughtiness sense.

sources.title: 長（読み）チョウ｜コトバンク（デジタル大辞泉・精選版 日本国語大辞典・普及版 字通）
sources.summary_en: Digital Daijisen lists a sense of 長 as ‘lengthen; grow bigger’ and includes 増長 among its examples. The National Dictionary also lists a colloquial 長 meaning ‘presumptuous’ but labels it as possibly abbreviated from 増長, so that sense does not establish an independent contribution to the compound.

sources.title: ゾウチョウ｜言葉｜漢字ペディア
sources.summary_en: Defines 増長 as a tendency or degree becoming stronger, and as presumptuousness or gradually becoming haughty; notes that it often applies to undesirable things.

sources.title: 増｜漢字一字｜漢字ペディア
sources.summary_en: Lists 増 as ‘increase’ and also ‘be arrogant/get presumptuous’ in 増長. Its character-formation note attributes the graph explanation to 角川新字源 and describes 増’s ‘increase’ meaning; it does not analyze the compound’s history.

claims.text_en: Modern dictionary definitions support understanding 増長 as a degree or tendency becoming stronger and, in the relevant personal sense, someone gradually becoming haughty or presumptuous. Thus the example’s ‘grow arrogant’ gloss fits the established compound meaning.

A modern kanji reference gives 長 a ‘lengthen; grow bigger’ sense and lists 増長 as an example. This supports associating 長 with growth or increase in degree in the compound, but the reference does not explicitly analyze the compound’s morpheme-by-morpheme semantics. The sources do not support treating 長 alone as meaning ‘arrogant.’

The references also associate 増 itself with ‘arrogant/get presumptuous’ in 増長, so the consulted material does not establish a clean division in which 増 means only ‘increase’ and 長 alone contributes the growth aspect to the modern compound.

The National Dictionary cites a general intensification example from 宝物集 (c. 1179) and cites 日葡辞書 (1603–04) for the haughtiness sense. These are dictionary-recorded Japanese usage attestations; they do not prove the compound’s historical formation or derivation.

sources.title: 掻く(カク)とは？ 意味や使い方 | コトバンク（精選版 日本国語大辞典・デジタル大辞泉）
sources.summary_en: The dictionary places rubbing/scratching and the outward-expression group under one 掻く headword. The latter includes emitting sweat or snoring, with a Heike Monogatari citation for 高いびきかいて臥したりけるが. Its editorial note says this group is semantically far from the physical-action senses and tentatively suggests that outward signs of discomfort or pain may underlie it. That is an expressly conjectural bridge, not an established derivation.

sources.title: かく | 同訓異義 | 漢字ペディア
sources.summary_en: This orthographic reference groups 搔く usage examples including いびきを搔く with scratching, cutting, gathering, and bringing something outward. It supports the conventional written association but does not establish historical unity or a semantic derivation.

claims.text_en: The modern dictionaries consulted list ‘scratch/rub’ and ‘emit outward,’ including snoring, under the same 掻く headword. This supports presenting snoring as an established conventional use of 掻く; it does not by itself settle whether the uses are historically one verb or homonyms.

The dictionary gives 高いびきかいて臥したりけるが from Heike Monogatari as a citation for the ‘emit outward’ sense. It describes that sense group as semantically distant from the physical-action senses and only conjectures a connection through outward signs of bodily discomfort or pain.

For a reusable modern explanation, いびきをかく is a conventional way to say ‘snore’ or ‘make snoring sounds’; a literal ‘scratch’ interpretation is unsupported. The reviewed sources do not establish how this construction developed historically from the physical-action sense.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 庭 (にわ) means a garden or yard: an outdoor space associated with a home or other place. It can refer to a planted garden or to the surrounding grounds more generally.

senses.definition: to this extent; this much; so much

meaning_guide.explanation_en: これほど means “to this extent” or “this much.” これ points to a degree or amount as “this,” and ほど marks its extent.

parts.contribution_en: Points to a degree or amount as “this.”

senses.definition: A rhetorical question expressing disbelief or incredulity, roughly “could that really be?”

meaning_guide.explanation_en: ものか presents the preceding plain-form clause as a possibility and asks about it rhetorically: “Could that really be so?” The question conveys disbelief, as the speaker treats that possibility as hard to accept.

parts.contribution_en: Turns the preceding clause into a possibility under consideration, roughly “such a thing.”
Marks the possibility as a question; here the question conveys disbelief.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 大胆 combines 大, “great,” with 胆, “nerve” or “courage,” giving the idea of great nerve: boldness or audacity. The suffix さ turns 大胆 into a noun for that quality.

parts.contribution_en: adds the sense of greatness or degree

senses.definition: to be surprised; to be startled

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 驚く means to feel surprise or alarm in response to something unexpected. It can describe a sudden startle or a broader feeling of surprise.

純粋 describes something as free from mixture with something of another kind, hence pure or unmixed. 純 contributes the idea of purity, while 粋 reinforces it with the sense of what is essential and unadulterated.

senses.definition: to illuminate; to shine light on

senses.definition: a state of being completely absorbed or engrossed

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 額（ひたい）means the forehead, the upper front part of the head above the eyes.

senses.definition: A pattern using a verb in dictionary form + ように to describe something as if it were doing that action; 射るように means “as if to pierce.”

senses.definition: to be astonished; to be appalled

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 呆れる（あきれる）means to be so surprised or shocked that you are left speechless. It often suggests disbelief or disapproval, giving it the sense “to be appalled”; the reaction can also be simple astonishment.
どうせ means “anyway” or “in any case.” It presents a situation or outcome as unchanged by other possibilities, often with a resigned or dismissive tone.

senses.definition: A sentence-ending pattern that asserts something while inviting agreement or emphasizing the speaker’s realization.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: In ではないか, ではない makes a negative copular statement and か turns it into a question. As a sentence ending, this negative question often invites agreement or conveys the speaker’s realization, depending on intonation and context.

senses.definition: The negative ずに pattern means “without doing” the verb; 負けずに means “without losing” or “without being outdone.”

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 負けずに uses the stem of 負ける, “to lose” or “to be outdone,” with ずに to mark that action as not happening while another action proceeds. The pattern is somewhat more formal or literary than ないで; here it means “without losing” or “without being outdone.”

senses.definition: such; of that kind; like that

senses.definition: An informal, typically masculine first-person pronoun: I; me.

senses.definition: A sentence-final particle that adds emphasis or presents a statement as information for the listener.

sources.title: 亭(テイ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク
sources.summary_en: Digital Daijisen gives 亭 senses including a rest pavilion, residence, lodging place, and building where food, drink, or entertainment draws guests. Nihon Kokugo Daijiten separately records 亭 as a household head, with an example from 1430. These Japanese usage records do not establish how the compound 亭主 developed.

sources.title: 亭 | 漢字一字 | 漢字ペディア
sources.summary_en: Defines 亭 as an inn, restaurant, or teahouse, as well as a pavilion. Its character formation note describes a building where people stop and rest; this is a character-level account, not evidence for the historical formation of 亭主.

sources.title: 主(シュ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク
sources.summary_en: Digital Daijisen defines 主 read as シュ as a person who hosts guests at home or is central to ownership or control, and defines あるじ as a household head or group head. Nihon Kokugo Daijiten records a separate ぬし sense for a husband or male partner, with a Kokin Wakashū example dated 905–914.

sources.title: 亭主(テイシュ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク
sources.summary_en: Digital Daijisen defines 亭主 as the master of a household, especially an inn or teahouse, a husband, and a tea host. Nihon Kokugo Daijiten gives separate examples for household head (1180), shopkeeper (1563), husband (1763–69), and tea host (1211). The entry documents senses and attestations, not the semantic pathway between them.

sources.title: テイシュ | 言葉 | 漢字ペディア
sources.summary_en: Defines 亭主 as a household master, especially an inn or teahouse proprietor; a husband; and a person who serves tea to guests at a tea gathering.

sources.title: 主 | 漢字一字 | 漢字ペディア
sources.summary_en: Defines 主 as an owner, master, or head, and lists 亭主 as a compound. This supports a modern component gloss but does not give the historical development of the compound.

claims.text_en: As a modern component-based explanation, 亭 can evoke a lodging or establishment such as an inn or teahouse, while 主 contributes the person who owns, heads, or hosts for it. This is a supported explanatory reading of the component senses alongside the compound’s dictionary definition; the opened dictionaries do not explicitly establish this as the compound’s historical derivation.

Japanese dictionaries directly record 亭主 for a household head and, especially, an inn or teahouse proprietor. Nihon Kokugo Daijiten cites a household-head example from 1180 and an innkeeper example from 1563.

亭主 is also directly recorded with the sense “husband”; Nihon Kokugo Daijiten cites an example from 1763–69. The sources opened here do not establish the specific semantic pathway from household head or proprietor to husband.

A separate Japanese reading of 主, ぬし, is recorded with the sense “husband” or “male partner,” including a Kokin Wakashū example dated 905–914. This is a different reading and does not establish that it produced the husband sense of 亭主.

本当 describes something as true, actual, or genuine, rather than false or merely apparent. In 本当の + noun and 本当に, it conveys “real/genuine” and “really/truly,” respectively.

claims.text_en: Modern 本当 covers being factual rather than false, actual rather than apparent, and genuine; dictionaries also record related senses of originalness or proper state. These are whole-word senses, not evidence that 本 and 当 each contribute an identifiable part of the meaning.

In 本当の + noun, context can yield ‘a real instance, not a counterfeit’ or ‘a prototypical or ideal instance.’ This offers a contextual semantic relation between genuineness and what counts as a true instance, but the study does not derive that relation from separate contributions of 本 and 当.

A scholarly review of the historical literature reports that the etymology of ほんとう remains unsettled, including proposed relations to ほん and 本途物也. Those proposals do not establish a historical derivation or the modern semantic contribution of 当.

本統 is recorded with the reading ほんとう, and 本途 is recorded with senses related to 本当. These records establish alternate written forms and lexical associations, but do not by themselves prove a derivation or a component-based explanation of modern 本当.

claims.text_en: In current usage 間違える includes both making an error and taking one thing for another. In the supplied example 別の本と間違えた, the verb has the latter sense: the speaker treated another book as the intended one.

A common modern distinction is that 間違う focuses on being outside a correct or expected state, whereas 間違える often focuses on confusing one item with another. The distinction is a tendency; both forms can be used in many of the same contexts.

For the incorrect-result sense, one linguistic analysis treats 間違う as intransitive and 間違える as its transitive counterpart. The dictionary entries also associate 違う and 違える through senses involving difference and error. These sources support a modern semantic relationship among the verbs, but do not by themselves prove that 間違える was historically formed by adding 間 to 違える.

These are the dictionary’s cited first examples for むめい senses, not proof of the word’s origin.

The dictionary separately records むみょう as a reading of 無名 and gives older attestations under that reading. Those attestations should not be treated as evidence that the modern むめい reading or its ‘not publicly known’ sense originated at the same time.

claims.text_en: A Japanese character dictionary lists one sense of 分 as 'state, degree, or manner' and gives 気分 as an example. This supports a broad state-like association for the character in this compound, but does not demonstrate that modern speakers assign 分 a distinct, independently recoverable contribution in 気分, much less a specific 'sick/unwell' meaning.

Dictionaries define 気分 at the word level as a mind-body state or feeling; one modern sub-sense concerns feelings arising from bodily condition. 気分が悪い can therefore mean feeling physically unwell without requiring a separate gloss for 分.

The Seisenban Nihon Kokugo Daijiten records a separate sense of 気分 meaning being unwell or ill and cites a 1229 吾妻鏡 example. This is evidence for historical use of the whole word, not for a historical derivation from the isolated character sense of 分.

claims.text_en: Modern Japanese dictionaries define 気持ち as feelings or thoughts held toward something, a resulting state of mind, or one's mental stance. These are whole-word definitions, not a component-by-component analysis.

A modern dictionary lists 気 senses including mental activity in response to things, mood, and feeling. These senses make a mental-state association for 気 relevant to 気持ち, but do not prove a specific contribution within that word.

持つ can mean holding something in one's mind, such as worries or a dream. This supports a possible modern association with having or holding a feeling, but does not show that this is the specific contribution of 持ち in 気持ち.

The dictionary history for 気持ち records its textual use and later overlap with 心持. Those historical notes attest usage and semantic development; they do not establish a derivation from separately identified component meanings.

The National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics describes forms perceived by contemporary speakers as fixed single words rather than two-verb compounds, giving 落ち着く with 気分 as an example. This cautions against treating the calmness sense as a transparent sum of 落ちる and 着く.
Whole-word dictionary entries define 落ち着く as becoming stable, quiet, or calm when disturbance subsides; an NINJAL entry gives 気分が落ち着いた as an example. This supports the supplied sense.

As standalone verbs, 落ちる includes moving downward, and 着く includes reaching a destination or position. These meanings do not, by themselves, show how either verb contributes to the calmness sense of 落ち着く.

sources.summary_en: The NINJAL IPAL verb reference lists 付く patterns by sense and argument structure. Its examples include 彼はその事について想像が付いていた under a 付く pattern. This independently supports 想像が付く as an established construction, but the single example does not establish how freely novel nouns can occur in that pattern.

claims.text_en: The dictionary evidence attests mental interpretations in particular expressions: 気が付く can mean ‘think of, notice, realize,’ and 心付く can mean that something outside awareness becomes conscious. These support explaining the mental reading in those expressions; they do not show that bare 付く independently has a general ‘come to mind’ meaning.

A result/state use of 付く is also attested with mental content: the dictionary entries give 想像がつく and 解釈の付かなかった問題, and NINJAL’s IPAL reference gives 想像が付いていた. This shows that the relevant use is not limited to 気が付く, while the cited evidence remains tied to particular constructions.

The sources distinguish noticing or awareness from reaching a result or conclusion. For a reusable explanation, ‘come to mind’ should therefore be presented with its construction or context, rather than as a broad gloss for 付く on its own.

sources.title: 慢 — 新纂浄土宗大辞典
sources.summary_en: This Buddhist dictionary defines 慢 as looking down on others in conceit and identifies it with Sanskrit māna. It lists 我慢 among the seven types of conceit and glosses the Buddhist term as taking one’s body and mind to be eternal and unchanging.

sources.title: DILA Glossaries for Buddhist Studies — 我慢
sources.summary_en: The opened page aggregates Buddhist dictionary entries. One identifies 我慢 with Sanskrit Asmimāna and glosses it as relying on the self and becoming conceited; another gives pride or arrogance and cites Buddhist textual usage. The entries support the Buddhist sense, not a modern Japanese character-by-character derivation.

sources.title: Vibhaṅga, Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅga, (66) Asmimāno — E-Piṭak
sources.summary_en: The opened Pali text presents asmimāna in a Buddhist doctrinal passage with repeated 'I am' formulations and identifies the resulting conceit or assertion as asmimāna. It attests a Buddhist conceptual use, not the later Japanese semantic change.

claims.text_en: Modern Japanese dictionaries define 我慢 as a whole word meaning to endure or bear something. They do not say that the modern meaning is composed from independent modern meanings of 我 and 慢.

The documented Japanese semantic sequence is Buddhist self-centered conceit → asserting one’s will or obstinacy → enduring or bearing something. The Seisenban Nihon Kokugo Daijiten explicitly presents this sequence as a likely explanation rather than a proven derivation, and its earliest cited example for the endurance sense is from 1782.

In the Buddhist term, the references associate 我慢 with asmi-māna or asmimāna and describe the concept in terms of selfhood or self-consciousness and conceit. They do not establish that the characters contribute separately to the modern Japanese sense 'endurance.'

claims.text_en: A restrained gloss of the written components is possible: dictionaries associate 馳 with making a horse run or rushing, and 走 with running or dashing. Those character meanings do not show that modern speakers derive 馳走’s hospitality or food sense compositionally from the two characters. In current use, the word’s hospitality and meal meanings should be explained as established word senses.

Japanese lexicographic evidence supports an early 馳走 sense of running about: Nihon Kokugo Daijiten gives that sense and a dated example from 1096. It next lists a sense of looking after or caring for someone, with an example dated 1114. These entries support a historical semantic connection to running about, but do not by themselves establish that the Japanese word was formed specifically from the modern verbs 馳せる and 走る.

Nihon Kokugo Daijiten explains the hospitality sense as arising from running about to make preparations and defines it as heartfelt hospitality, especially hospitality involving a meal, or the food served. Its cited example for that sense is dated 1604–08. Digital Daijisen gives a similar preparation-based explanation. This is dictionary support for the semantic development; it does not document every intermediate step or independently prove a particular morphological derivation.

The opened entry for 馳せる supports that it can mean running quickly or making a horse or vehicle run quickly, and records its historical relation to はしる. It does not state that 馳走 was created by combining 馳せる with 走る. The proposed specific formation remains unverified.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 写す means to make a copy or reproduction of something, so the result follows or represents the original. The word can describe copying text or reproducing an image.

component_uses.contribution_en: “Copy” or “reproduce”; names the action that is being recommended or expected.

senses.definition: A level, standard, or arrangement; the usual or ordinary state.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 並み can mean a row or arrangement, or the level at which things stand alongside one another. From this idea of comparison, it also means an ordinary or standard level; in 人並み, for example, it means an ordinary level by human standards.

component_uses.contribution_en: arrangement, here the way the fur lies

senses.definition: Laughter; the act or sound of laughing.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 笑い（わらい）is the noun use of 笑う（わらう）’s continuative form. It refers to laughing as an act or to the sound of laughter.

parts.contribution_en: The continuative form of 笑う used as a noun for laughing or laughter.

component_uses.contribution_en: laughter

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 二百 means “two hundred.” 二 contributes the quantity two, and 百 supplies the hundred-unit, giving 2 × 100.

parts.contribution_en: the quantity two
the hundred-unit

component_uses.contribution_en: Two hundred.

senses.definition: Cleaning; the act of removing dirt or disorder.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 掃除 means cleaning: clearing away dirt or mess from a place or object. 掃 contributes sweeping or clearing, and 除 contributes removing; together they frame cleaning as clearing away what is unwanted, though cleaning can be done in ways other than sweeping.

parts.contribution_en: Sweep or clear away.
Remove what is unwanted.

component_uses.contribution_en: Means cleaning; with 大, it refers to cleaning on an extensive scale.

senses.definition: A sigh; a breath let out audibly, often expressing weariness or emotion.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: ため息 is an audible breath let out as a sigh, often expressing weariness or emotion. ため suggests breath being held or building up, while 息 means breath; together they present a sigh as breath released after it has been held in.

parts.contribution_en: Suggests breath held or built up before release, as in 溜める.
Breath; here, the breath released as a sigh.

component_uses.contribution_en: a sigh

senses.definition: Shade or shadow; protection or help attributed to someone or something.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 陰（かげ）means shade or shadow: an area screened from light. The image of being sheltered in shade extends to unseen protection or support from someone or something, as in お陰（おかげ）.

component_uses.contribution_en: Also means protection, help, or benefit in modern Japanese; these meanings connect with おかげ’s helpful sense.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 短い means short in length or duration: something extends only a little way or lasts only a little time.

component_uses.contribution_en: The く-form of 短い (“short”), supplying the state that changes.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 幼稚（ようち）refers to early childhood and to a childish, immature quality. Both parts carry the idea of youth; together they describe an early stage of development, and the word often criticizes something as not mature enough.

parts.contribution_en: young; in an early stage of life
young or immature

component_uses.contribution_en: early childhood; referring to very young children

senses.definition: An end, limit, or point at which something is cut off.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 切り names the point where something is cut off, giving it an end or limit. It can also mark the boundary after which a period, amount, or sequence does not continue.

parts.contribution_en: The point where something is cut off: its end or limit.

component_uses.contribution_en: cutoff, limit, or endpoint
end or limit

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 打つ（うつ）means to strike or hit something, making contact with it with a blow or similar force.

component_uses.contribution_en: The combining form of 打つ, adding a sense of forceful action.

senses.definition: To defeat someone; cause someone to lose.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 負かす means to beat or defeat someone, making them lose. It is transitive: the person defeated is typically marked with を, and the verb commonly describes winning against an opponent in a contest.

component_uses.contribution_en: Means to make someone lose, forming the core idea of defeating.

senses.definition: To lose or be defeated; to be outdone.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 負ける means to lose or be defeated when another side prevails. It also means to be outdone when someone or something proves superior in a comparison.

component_uses.contribution_en: The stem of 負ける, “to lose” or “to be outdone.”

senses.definition: To leave or go away from a place.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 去る（さる）means to leave a place or go away from it. It can describe a person or a thing departing.

component_uses.contribution_en: To go away; it makes the departure from a place explicit.

senses.definition: Unease or anxiety; a feeling of uncertainty or worry.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 不安 means worry or anxiety that leaves someone unable to feel settled. 安 contributes the idea of being calm or settled; 不’s role in the word is unresolved.

parts.contribution_en: Its contribution to 不安 is unresolved.
Contributes the idea of being calm or settled.

sources.title: 不安(フアン)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク
sources.summary_en: The Digital Daijisen defines 不安 as being worried and unable to feel settled. The Nihon Kokugo Daijiten gives a similar definition and lists a 1428 quotation as its earliest example under that sense. The page also distinguishes other homographic senses, including 不和 and bodily illness.

sources.title: 安(アン)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク
sources.summary_en: Digital Daijisen lists 安 as meaning calm or settled in one sense. The Nihon Kokugo Daijiten’s 1428 quotation under another 安 entry glossed as 案 shows that the character sequence in an old quotation should not by itself be taken as evidence for the modern compound’s history.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, Japanese dictionaries define 不安 as worry or concern accompanied by an inability to feel settled.

安 has a dictionary-listed sense of being calm or settled. This supports that component’s present-day semantic contribution, but the opened references do not establish a complete historical derivation of 不安.

The Nihon Kokugo Daijiten lists a 1428 quotation as the earliest example under its modern 不安 sense. The separate 安 entry also associates the quotation’s 安 with 案; the quotation alone therefore does not prove when the modern word arose or how it was historically formed.

senses.definition: To shoot or launch an arrow or other projectile.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 射る means to shoot or launch an arrow or another projectile toward a target. It describes sending the projectile outward, often with a bow.

senses.definition: To accumulate or store something; to hold something back.

meaning_guide.explanation_en: 溜める means to cause something to accumulate or keep it in reserve, often by not using or releasing it yet. It can describe money or energy being saved, work piling up, or feelings being held in.
